subject: Post-demo alignment: approval trajectory & proposed MAP
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@cardinalhealth.ai>, Marco Ruiz <marco@cardinalhealth.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Post-demo alignment: approval trajectory & proposed MAP

Hi Sara / Marco — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the POC approval: 

1) Decision makers & timeline we heard today:
- Economic buyer: Sara Lin (confirmed) — primary approver for budget & contract
- Security/compliance: Marco / procurement loop (SOC2 evidence required, encryption/KMS Qs)
- Technical approver: ML infra team (you mentioned a short review by the platform team)

2) Minimal acceptance criteria you outlined:
- Privacy: no PHI stored beyond token-level ephemeral cache
- Latency: 95th pct < 300ms for inference on 2k token context
- Cost target: < $0.03 per 1k tokens (ballpark)

3) Proposed MAP (attached initial draft) — milestones I put in the workbook: discovery signoff (this week), security questionnaire & evidence (2 weeks), POC deployment + smoke tests (3–4 weeks), executive approval + contract (5–6 weeks).

I attached a lightweight MAP (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx) with owners and dates. Please confirm: 1) that Sara is the right economic owner to track approvals, 2) Marco should own security evidence collection, and 3) whether procurement needs a separate milestone for terms/PO.

If you like, I can convert MAP into a shared GDrive and our CSM will enter the milestones in HubSpot.

Next steps (my ask):
- Sara: confirm approval owner(s) and target approval week
- Marco: flag any immediate evidence gaps (SOC2 artifacts you need)
- Marco/Sara: availability for an internal 30-min security sync this week

Thanks — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@cardinalhealth.ai>

Thanks Vivek — great demo and clean recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: I will be the economic approver. Final sign-off for budget will come from our VP of Data (cc'd below once formal review starts).
- Marco is our security contact and will lead the evidence collection. He asked that you send a short summary of SOC2 artifacts (scope, retention, subservice orgs) — that will speed his checklist.
- Procurement: we do prefer receiving a draft SOW + estimated TCO before we start legal/PO. Procurement will ask for an approved SOW + a purchase order to start payment terms.

On timing: target approval week is currently 2026-07-20 — aggressive but possible if SOC2 answers and SOW are quick.

We can do a 30-min security sync Friday 06/18 at 10:00am ET — Marco, does that work?

Quick note on acceptance criteria: the latency threshold you noted looks fine for our initial tests, but the ML infra team will want to run a 1k/2k token workload to validate.

Thanks — Sara

Sara Lin

Thanks Marco — attaching a compact SOC2 evidence summary (SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf) and a short Q&A doc we use for procurement. I also uploaded an editable MAP to our shared drive and attached the initial workbook here (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx).

Notes on the artifacts: 
- Encryption: we support customer KMS (BYOK) and default AES-256 at rest; details in the attached summary.
- Data residency: hosted regions can be scoped to US-only on Dedicated or Private deployments — we call that out in the SOW template.
- Incident response: standard SLAs + war-room escalation process (summary included).

Priya / Rishi — can you review the MAP owners column and suggest any changes to the timelines? I want to make sure we don't overpromise the POC window given our Dedicated capacity planning.

Vivek

- Add Rishi as owner for the infra validation step (he'll coordinate the test harness and provide the 1k/2k token results).
